reason: A fruiting head is an infructescence. The head form is extra detail, not a contradiction. The described qualities (width, pendulous) apply to the whole infructescence, so the bearer is correct even though the shape word is not kept.
Same as R3283: a fruit head is an infructescence, and the bearer is correct.
Plural of fruiting head. Same as R3283.

Corolla lip (FLOPO_0985017) is right for the lower lip of a two-lipped corolla. Lamiaceae and Scrophulariaceae floras also give calyx lips, and an orchid lip is the labellum. Restrict the rule to corolla wholes, as done for 'lower lip lobe'.
Same as R3286: 'lower lip' is also used for the calyx (Lamiaceae) and the orchid labellum. Corolla lip is correct only when the whole is the corolla.

PO_0009038 is the real PO class 'palea' (checked in plant_ontology.obo). 'palea' as a synonym of inflorescence bract only covers the chaff scales of Asteraceae. The quality rule R2138 already maps the presence statement to palea + present. This bearer rule is consistent with it and harmless.

All 584 statements come from one Cyperaceae flora, where a floral scale is the bract (glume) that subtends a single flower in the spikelet. That is an inflorescence bract. The perianth-scale and Juncaceae readings do not occur in this source.
Plural of floral scale. Same as R3289.

In the source (Myristicaceae, Knema: 'staminal disc flat, subcircular') the staminal disc is the disc-shaped fused androecium, which matches the synandrium definition (an androecium with fused stamens and anthers). It is not the nectar disc, which is floral disc FLOPO_0986025. The first check assumed the nectar-disc sense.
Same source and use as R3294: the androecial disc of Knema is the fused androecium.

A calycophyll is a calyx lobe enlarged into a leaf-like blade. Mapping a kind of part to its parent class is acceptable for a bearer. Its shape, size, colour and hairs are correctly qualities of a calyx lobe.
The bearer is a calyx lobe. The word 'enlarged' is not kept, but nothing false is stated. The described qualities apply to the calyx lobe.

In the source, the counted strands have sclerified sheaths, so they are whole vascular bundles. A single xylem-only or phloem-only strand does not occur in this flora's use. A part constraint would not separate those senses anyway.
Plural of vascular strand. Same as R3298.
Lime-secreting pits on Saxifraga leaves are hydathodes, but the chalk glands of Plumbaginaceae are salt glands, not hydathodes. The gland class (PO synonym 'gland') is correct for both.
A laminar colleter is a colleter. Its position on the leaf blade is context, which the rule already records (container leaf lamina PO_0020039 in its note). The bearer class is correct.
Plural of laminar colleter. Same as R3311.
Woolly hairs are trichomes. The statements give colour and other qualities of the hairs. Woolliness, where it matters, is a separate quality word ('woolly' or 'lanate'). The bearer is not wrong.
Calicle bracts are extra outer involucral bracts in Asteraceae heads, for example Senecio. In Malvaceae the same word means an epicalyx segment (FLOPO_0986038). Restrict the rule to head contexts.
French form of R3318. Same family-dependent sense, so restrict it to capitulum (capitule) contexts.
Same as R3318. Outside Asteraceae heads it is an epicalyx segment.

A pseudolocule is a cavity made by a secondary false septum (Vaccinium), not a true locule of the carpel. Mapping it to locule would turn '10-pseudoloculed' into 10 locules, which is false (5 true locules). It needs its own class or no rule.
Same as R3327: a false locule is not a locule, and mapping it would give wrong locule counts.
This is an adjective (having false locules), not a part name. Like R3327, it must not count as locules, so it should also not be added to flora_counted_parts.tsv.

In the source, 'perianth blade' is the blade of a free perianth segment (short-oblong, acute, incurved). Those shape words describe the tepal. There is no tepal-blade class, so tepal is the closest existing bearer. The first check's fused-perianth reading does not fit the source.
Same as R3332. The blade part is lost, but the shape of the segment blade is the tepal shape as floras describe it, and no blade class exists.

In the source ('93–126 par capitule', hermaphrodite) these are Asteraceae disc flowers, so disk flower (PO_0025332) is correct there. In cymes or umbels 'fleur centrale' is just the middle flower. Restrict the rule to head contexts.

The statements describe separate members of a floral corona (ovate, bifid, spatulate, 6 mm long). The corona lobe definition, 'one of the divisions of a floral corona', with synonym 'coronal scale', fits them.
Same as R3337. In floras, 'coronal appendage' names the separate members of the corona, as 'coronal scale' does.
A tack-shaped gland is a gland (PO synonym). The shape word is not kept, but the bearer is correct, as already accepted for the 'tack-gland' rules R3339 and R3340.
